cas: ═══ Computer Algebra System (CAS) ═══
JC2 features a powerful, exact Computer Algebra System for symbolic mathematics.
★ The Boundary: Numerical vs. Symbolic Computation
JC2 strictly separates Numerical and Symbolic domains:
• Numerical (Default): Variables hold values (x = 5). Expressions evaluate
immediately to numbers, matrices, or fractions.
• Symbolic (CAS): Variables hold AST nodes (x = sym("x")). Expressions
build algebraic trees instead of evaluating.
You cross from Numerical → Symbolic by using `sym("x")` or string variables.
You cross from Symbolic → Numerical by using `evalf()`, `subs()`, or `toFunc()`.
★ Automatic Symbolic Promotion
• Fractional Powers: Exact integers or fractions raised to fractional powers
(e.g., 2^(1/2)) no longer degrade to floating-point `double`. If they cannot
be evaluated exactly, they automatically promote to a Symbolic expression.
• Function Nodes: Only standard built-in math functions (sin, cos, exp, log,
sqrt, etc.) can be captured as symbolic nodes (`SymFunc`). Passing a symbolic
variable to a user-defined function or an incompatible built-in will either
evaluate it immediately or throw a TypeError.
Symbolic Variables & Expressions
x = sym("x")                 Create a symbolic variable
expr = x^2 + 2*x + 1         Build exact symbolic expressions
subs(expr, x, 5)             Substitute x with 5 → 36 (Strings like "x" also work!)
subs(x + y, [x, y], [1, 2])  Multiple substitution
★ Variable Name Inputs
All CAS functions (diff, integ, limit, solveEq, taylor, polyDiv, etc.) now
accept direct symbolic variables instead of just strings.
Example: diff(x^2, x) is perfectly equivalent to diff(x^2, "x").

factor(x^4 - 1)              → (x - 1) * (x + 1) * (x^2 + 1) (Cantor-Zassenhaus)

of the polynomial `poly`. Essential for exact symbolic
integration of rational functions.
Calculus (Exact Symbolic)
diff(sin(x^2), x)            → 2 * x * cos(x^2)
integ(exp(x^2), x)           → Risch Algorithm (Liouvillian extensions)
integ(x^2, x, 0, 1)          → 1/3 (Definite integral)
verifyInteg(expr, x)         → true if diff(integ(expr, x), x) == expr, else false
limit(sin(x)/x, x, 0)        → 1 (Gruntz asymptotic expansion algorithm)
limit(1/x, x, 0, "-")        → -oo (Left-sided limit)

Equation Solving
solveEq(x^2 - 2, x)          → @[sqrt(2), -sqrt(2)] (Exact roots!)
solveEq(x^3 - 1, x)          → @[1, E^(2/3 * PI * i), E^(4/3 * PI * i)] (All complex roots!)
★ Constants & Limitations:
• PI and E are now parsed as exact symbolic constants in the CAS engine
to prevent premature floating-point evaluation.
• solveEq now exactly solves high-degree binomial equations (ax^n + b = 0),
returning all complex roots using Euler's formula (E and PI).
• For high-degree irreducible polynomials, solveEq returns exact `RootOf`
algebraic number nodes. For robust numerical root-finding, use `solveE`.

Defining Functions
f(x) = sin(x) + x^2                Single variable
g(x, y) = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)          Multi variable
h(a, b) = { t = a+b; t^2 }         Block body (auto-local t)

const f(x) = x^2                   Immutable function
ref f(x) = x^2                     Modify outer function
state f(x) = x^2                   Private persistent function
Functions are compiled into bytecode closures executed by the VM.
They automatically capture the surrounding scope at definition time.
★ Recursion: Local functions automatically capture their own name by reference,
allowing them to safely call themselves recursively.
Built-in Function Overloading
You can define a user function with the same name as a built-in,
as long as the parameter count is DIFFERENT:
exp(a, b, c) = a + b + c     ✓ OK (built-in exp takes 1 arg)
exp(x) = x                   ✗ Error (conflicts with built-in arity)
When calling, built-in functions always take priority if the argument
count matches a built-in signature.
Calculus (Symbolic & Numerical)
JC2 supports both exact symbolic calculus (via the CAS engine) and
high-performance numerical approximations.
Symbolic (Exact):

integ(x^2, x)        → 1/3 * x^3

scope: ═══ Variable Scoping & Protection Rules ═══
★ Scope Modifiers Quick Summary
Modifier | Scope Bound | Memory Lifecycle       | Capture Semantics
(none)   | Function    | Destroyed on return    | Auto-Local (Shadows outer)
local    | Block {}    | Destroyed on block end | Strict Block Isolation
ref      | Outer/Global| Tied to outer variable | Mutates outer directly
state    | Closure     | Persistent across calls| Private State Machine
Default Behaviors
• Top Level (REPL): Variables are global. Blocks ({}, for, while) do NOT
create isolated scopes by default.
• Inside Functions: New assignments are Auto-Local to the function.
They survive block boundaries but are destroyed when the function returns.
Strict Block Scope (local)
Restricts a variable strictly to the current block ({}, if, for, while).
if (true) { local temp = 100 }
print(temp)  // ✗ Error: temp is undefined
• Variable Routing: Ordinary assignments (y = 2) inside blocks bypass the
block and attach to the function/global scope. Only `local` traps them.
• Closure Safety: If a closure captures a `local` variable, its physical
memory lives on inside the closure, but its name is destroyed.
Upward Scope Resolution (ref)
Binds a variable to an OUTER scope variable across function boundaries.
counter = 0
bump() = ref counter += 1      // Modifies outer 'counter' directly
• Capture Semantics: Local variables are captured by physical memory.
Global variables are captured by name (late-binding).
• Standalone: `ref a;` binds to outer `a`. Throws immediately if undefined.
• Parameters: `addOne(ref x) = { x += 1 }` forces pass-by-reference.
Closures & State Semantics (state)
Gives a closure PRIVATE PERSISTENT memory. The outer scope is untouched.
f() = { state n = 0; n += 1; return n }
• state x = expr  : Evaluates `expr` EXACTLY ONCE on the first call.
• state x += expr : Captures outer `x` once, adds `expr` ON EVERY CALL.
• Standalone      : `state a;` captures `a` EXACTLY at definition time.
Throws IMMEDIATELY at definition time if `a` is undefined.
Destructuring Modifiers
Each target variable can independently carry a scope modifier:
[ref a, state b, local c, d] = [1, 2, 3, 4]
{x: ref px, y: state py} = point
Namespaces (Dynamic Modules)
namespace Math {
local seed = 12345         // Private (not exported)
const PI = 3.14            // Public immutable
add(a, b) = a + b          // Public method
• Dynamic: Add/modify/delete members at runtime (Math.E = 2.718).
• Dict-Like: Supports keys(), values(), for-in loops.
• Freezing: `freeze(Math)` locks it, making it hashable.
Constants & Built-ins
• const: `const G = 9.81`. Cannot reassign, but can `delete`.
• System Constants: PI, E, i, I can be overwritten/deleted.
Restore via `resetConst()` or factory functions like `pi()`.
• Built-ins: Protected, but can be overloaded with a DIFFERENT arity.
`sin(a, b) = a + b` (OK), `sin(x) = x` (Error).
★ Variable Lifecycle Summary
Entity            Overwrite?   Delete?    Recover?
User variable     ✓            ✓          —
const variable    ✗            ✓          —
System constant   ✓            ✓          resetConst() / pi()
Built-in func     overload*    user only  automatic
* Only with a different parameter count

dict: ═══ Dictionary (Key-Value Store) ═══
Dicts store unordered key-value mappings in JC2. Keys can be ANY hashable type
(strings, numbers, instances with __hash__, or frozen containers). Values can
be of any type.
Creation
d = dict()                          Empty dictionary
d = {name: "Alice", age: 30}        Literal syntax (recommended)
d = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}    Quoted string keys also work
Shorthand Properties (Variables directly to Dict):
name = "Bob"; age = 25
d = { name, age }                 → {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}
For computed keys (using a variable's value as the key), wrap it in
parentheses or use the function form:
d = dict(dynamic_key, 42)         → {"[1]": 42}
Block vs. Dict Ambiguity Resolution
Because `{ ... }` is used for both code blocks and dictionaries, JC2 uses
a smart lookahead scanner to resolve ambiguities:
1. If it finds a colon `:` at the top level (ignoring ternary `? :`), it's a Dict.
{ [1, 2; 3, 4]: "matrix" }   → Dict
{ a ? b : c : "value" }      → Dict
2. If it finds a semicolon `;` at the top level, it's a Block.
{ a, b = 1; }                → Block
3. If neither is found, it checks for shorthand syntax:
{}                           → Empty Dict
{a, b}                       → Shorthand Dict {"a": a, "b": b}
{ a }                        → Shorthand Dict {"a": a}
* Tip: If you want a single-statement block that returns a variable,
always add a semicolon to avoid it being parsed as a shorthand dict:
{ a; }                       → Block returning 'a'
Access & Modification
d["key"]                            Read / Write the value
d["key"] += 1                       Compound assignment directly on the value
d - @{"key1", "key2"}               Key omission (returns a NEW Dict without the specified keys)
d - ["key1", "key2"]                Key omission using a List
d - {key1: 1}                       Key omission using another Dict (ignores values)
* Note: d[a] evaluates the variable 'a' and uses its value as the key.
If you want the literal string "a", use d["a"]. For convenience,
you can also use the dot operator: d.a (which is identical to d["a"]).
Dot Operator Syntax Sugar
The dot operator works identically to bracket syntax for string keys:
d.name                     → "Alice"     (same as d["name"])
d.age = 31                 → modifies    (same as d["age"] = 31)
d.score = 95               → adds new key

Reference Semantics & GC
Identical to Lists, Dicts are passed by reference.
d2 = d1
d2.a = 99                 // d1.a is now also 99
Dicts are fully tracked by the VM's Garbage Collector. Therefore, creating a
graph where Dict A points to Dict B, and Dict B points back to Dict A will
never cause a memory leak when they go out of scope.
Immutability & Hashing (Native Value Hashing)
JC2 uses a high-performance Native Value Hashing architecture.
Keys are hashed directly by their semantic value, meaning `1.0`, `int(1)`,
and `frac(1,1)` will all perfectly collide and map to the exact same key!
Keys MUST be hashable. Valid keys include:
• Numbers (double, int, Fraction, Complex, BaseNum)
• Strings and Symbolic Expressions
• Frozen containers (frozen List, Dict, Set)
• Functions, Classes, and Namespaces (hashed by reference)
• Class Instances (ONLY if frozen, or if they define a `__hash__` dunder method)

val(d)                              Returns a deep-copied, frozen snapshot.
hash(x)                             Returns the native hash value of x (as int).
Copying & Mutability Matrix
There is no "unfreeze" function. Use copying to change lock states:
Syntax        Depth         Lock State          Best For...

b = clone(a)  Deep          Fully unfrozen      Complete rebirth. Fully mutable nested data.

(If not defined, 'for-in' iterates over instance fields like a Dict)

to be used as a Dict key or Set element. (Must be paired with __eq__)
When calling methods explicitly (e.g., `p.foo()`), JC2 checks the instance's
own fields FIRST, then falls back to the class. This allows you to override
a method for a single instance:
p.dist = () => 0           // Overrides the class method for 'p' only
For implicit operations (like `a + b`, `hash(a)`, `str(a)`), JC2 strictly
bypasses instance fields and ONLY looks at the class definition. This
guarantees that all instances of a class share the exact same mathematical
and hashing behavior, keeping data structures safe.
p.__hash__ = () => 1       // Ignored by the built-in hash() function!
hash(p)                    // Implicit call: uses the Class's __hash__
Methods that return `self` enable fluent-style chaining:
add(x) = { self.parts = push(self.parts, x); return self }
Methods can return arrays/lists for destructured assignment:

match: The `match` expression provides powerful structural branching and destructuring.
It evaluates a subject and executes the first branch with a matching pattern.
• Pure identifiers (like `x` or `PI`) always BIND to a new local variable.
• To evaluate an expression and compare its result (Value Assertion), you MUST
enclose it in parentheses `()`. Static literals (1, "a", 2+3i) don't need parentheses.
Patterns are strictly evaluated from left to right. This allows dynamic
assertions to use variables that were just bound earlier in the SAME pattern!
[a, (2*a)] => "Matches if the second element is exactly twice the first!",
{"x": a, "y": (a^2)} => "Matches if y is the square of x!",
Matches Lists, RealMatrices, ComplexMatrices, and StringMatrices.
Uses `,` for rows and `;` for columns to strictly match dimensions.
[x, y]       // Matches 1x2 row vector or List of length 2
Extracts the remainder of a List, Matrix, or Dict.
The `...` pattern can be placed anywhere in a List or Matrix row.
It will dynamically capture all elements between the fixed head and tail.
[a, b, ...mid, c; ...res] => "Matches at least 3 cols, captures middle."
(Note: Only ONE rest pattern is allowed per row).
In matrices, `...` can capture either remaining COLUMNS in a row, or
remaining ROWS in the matrix, depending on its position:
• Before a semicolon `;`: Captures remaining COLUMNS for that specific row.
• At the very end before `]`: Captures all remaining ROWS as a sub-matrix.
// 'rest_col' is the rest of row 1 (row vector).
// 'rest_rows' is a matrix of all other rows.
[...row1; ...row2; ...res]      // 'row1' and 'row2' capture the first two rows.
Extracts values by key/field. Supports shorthand `{a}` for `{"a": a}`.
(Note: For Instances, it only matches data fields. For Namespaces, it matches everything including methods).
The `...rest` pattern always returns a standard Dict containing the remaining fields.
{name, age} if (age >= 18) => name + " is an adult",
Use `if` guard clauses with type predicates for type checking.
Patterns can be infinitely nested to extract deep data.
• Variables bound in a pattern are strictly local to that branch's body.
• Patterns are evaluated top-to-bottom. The first match wins.
• If no pattern matches, the expression safely returns `none`.
error: ═══ Error Handling & Tracebacks ═══
In JC2, errors generated by invalid math operations, type mismatches,
or explicit `throw` statements will terminate the current script sequence.
Throwing Errors
throw "message"             Throws an exact string error message
throw expr                  Throws any evaluated value
error("message")            Function form (acts exactly like `throw`)
Stack Traces (Tracebacks)
When an unhandled error or exception occurs, JC2's VM unwinds the
call stack and prints a highly detailed, ANSI-colorized Traceback.
This pinpoints the exact file, script line, and function where the
error originated, traversing seamlessly through class dunder methods
(__setitem__, etc.) and anonymous closures.
Try / Catch Blocks
try {
risky_code()
} catch (e) {
print("Caught an error:", e)
The `catch` variable (e.g., `e`) receives the error message as a string.
`try`/`catch` is an expression. It natively returns the value of the
`try` block if successful, or the value of the `catch` block if an error occurred.
Re-throwing & Control Flow
You can trigger `throw e` inside a catch block to bubble unhandled errors up.
Control flow signals (`break`, `continue`, and `return`) pass through
`try`/`catch` boundaries completely unaffected.
Protected Call (pcall)
`pcall(f)` provides a functional alternative to `try`/`catch`.
It executes a zero-argument function `f` and captures the result safely into a List.
Returns `@[1, result]` on success.
Returns `@[0, errorMsg]` on failure.
status = pcall(riskyFunc)
isError(status)       → true if error, false if success
Assertions
assert(cond)                  Throws if cond is falsy
assert(cond, "msg")           Throws custom message if falsy
assert("name", got, expected) Throws detailed mismatch error if got != expected

import: ═══ Import (Code Reuse & Native Modules) ═══
The `import` command loads code into the current environment.
It supports both JC2 script files (.jc2) and native C++ modules.
Syntax
import module               Loads module and binds it to a variable (Recommended)
import "path"               Loads and executes a .jc2 file without binding
★ Namespace Binding:
`import json` is syntax sugar for `json = import "json"`.
This keeps the global scope clean by isolating the module's contents.
Native Modules (built into the executable)
Native modules are written in C++ and compiled into JunkCalculator2.
They load instantly with zero file I/O overhead and are strictly isolated.
modules()                   List all available native modules
import moduleName           Load a native module into a namespace
Currently available:
image     BMP image generation & plotting
prob      11 probability distributions + hypothesis tests
json      JSON encode / decode / pretty-print
Native modules take priority over .jc2 files with the same name.
Importing the same module twice is a safe no-op (deduplicated).
Script Modules (.jc2 files)
import discrete             Loads discrete.jc2 into `discrete`
Smart Path Resolution (Script-Centric)
`import` resolves relative paths based on the directory of the
currently running script, NOT the terminal's working directory.
Search order for `import utils` inside C:/project/src/main.jc2:
1. C:/project/src/utils
2. C:/project/src/utils.jc2
3. C:/project/src/data/utils.jc2
4. C:/project/src/lib/utils.jc2
5. <workspace>/utils.jc2
6. <exe_dir>/lib/utils.jc2  (global fallback)
Once a library starts executing, its own directory becomes the
path context for any further imports or file operations within it.
Features & Safeguards
• Deduplication: Importing the same file/module twice is a no-op.
• Chained imports: A library can safely `import` other libraries.
• Error propagation: Errors inside an imported file abort the import.
• Encapsulation: All definitions are strictly isolated inside the returned Namespace.

The `image` module provides a high-performance 2D rasterization API backed
by C++. It allows rendering geometric shapes, statistical plots, and manipulating
pixels directly in memory, which can be encoded to BMP formats.

for thickness or coordinates. The engine will automatically perform

gcd.desc: Returns the greatest common divisor of a and b.

lcm.desc: Returns the least common multiple of a and b.

digits.desc: Returns the number of base-10 digits in an int.

isPrime.desc: Returns true if n is a prime number (via Miller-Rabin test), false otherwise.

nextPrime.desc: Returns the smallest prime number strictly greater than n.

nthPrime.desc: Returns the k-th prime number. Uses a mounted Prime.txt database if available, otherwise computes dynamically.

primePi.desc: Returns the number of primes less than or equal to n (Prime Counting Function).

phi.desc: Returns Euler's totient function (number of integers up to n that are coprime to n).

divisors.desc: Returns the number of positive divisors of n.

sigma.desc: Returns the sum of the k-th powers of the positive divisors of n. k defaults to 1.

omega.desc: Returns the number of distinct prime factors of n.

bigOmega.desc: Returns the total number of prime factors of n (counted with multiplicity).

mobius.desc: Returns the Möbius function of n: 0 if n has a squared prime factor, else (-1)^omega(n).

isPerfect.desc: Returns true if n is a perfect number (sum of proper divisors equals n), false otherwise.

mod.desc: Returns the mathematical modulo of a w.r.t b. The result is always non-negative.

C.desc: Returns the binomial coefficient (n choose k).

A.desc: Returns the number of k-permutations of n.

base.desc: Wraps an integer in a base-r display shell.

bnum.desc: Parses a string directly as a base-r number. For bases <= 36, uses alphanumeric chars (case-insensitive). For any base, use underscores to separate base-10 digit blocks.

changeBase.desc: Re-displays an existing BaseNum in a new base r.

data.desc: Strips the radix shell from a BaseNum, returning a plain int.

bitand.desc: Returns the bitwise AND of two numbers.

bitor.desc: Returns the bitwise OR of two numbers.

bitxor.desc: Returns the bitwise XOR of two numbers.

bitnot.desc: Returns the bitwise NOT of a number. If w is omitted, returns -a - 1. Otherwise, performs w-bit inversion.

bitshift.desc: Logical shift: Left if n > 0, Right if n < 0.

mean.desc: Returns the arithmetic mean of a dataset, or the theoretical mean of a Distribution.

var.desc: Returns the population variance of a dataset (divided by N), or the theoretical variance of a Distribution.

svar.desc: Returns the sample variance of a dataset (divided by N-1).

std.desc: Returns the population standard deviation of a dataset, or the theoretical standard deviation of a Distribution.

sstd.desc: Returns the sample standard deviation of a dataset.

max.desc: Returns the maximum value in a dataset or list.

min.desc: Returns the minimum value in a dataset or list.

span.desc: Returns the statistical range (max - min) of a dataset.

perc.desc: Returns the p-th percentile of a dataset (0 <= p <= 100).

median.desc: Returns the median (50th percentile) of a dataset.

mode.desc: Returns the mode(s) of a dataset. Returns a row vector if multimodal.

cov.desc: Returns the population covariance between two datasets.

corr.desc: Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient (r) between two datasets.

rsq.desc: Returns the coefficient of determination (R^2) between two datasets.

regress.desc: Performs linear regression Y = a + bX. Prints the model and returns @[a, b].

rand.desc: Returns a random continuous double. Defaults to [0, 1) if no arguments provided.

randint.desc: Returns a random discrete integer in the closed interval [min, max].

randc.desc: Returns a random complex number with real and imaginary parts in [min, max).

randmat.desc: Returns an r x c matrix of random continuous doubles.

randimat.desc: Returns an r x c matrix of random discrete integers. Defaults to [0, 10].

randcmat.desc: Returns an r x c matrix of random complex numbers.

magic.desc: Returns an n x n magic square matrix (n >= 3).

str.desc: Converts any value to a string representation. Calls __str__ on instances if available.

len.desc: Returns the length or element count of a string, vector, matrix, dict, list, or set.

substr.desc: Returns a substring starting at 'start'. If 'length' is provided, extracts that many characters.

replace.desc: Replaces all occurrences of 'old' with 'new' in string 's'.

format.desc: Formats a string using Python-style placeholders {}.

type.desc: Returns the type name of the given value as a string.

split.desc: Splits a string into a List of substrings using the specified delimiter.

join.desc: Joins elements of a list or array into a single string, separated by 'delim'.

list.desc: Constructs a heterogeneous List containing the provided arguments.

dict.desc: Constructs a Dictionary from key-value pairs.

set.desc: Constructs a Set containing unique elements. (Note: @{...} literal syntax is recommended).

push.desc: Appends a value to the end of a list or array.

pop.desc: Removes and returns the last element of a list (mutates) or array (returns last).

map.desc: Applies function f to each element of v. If only f is provided, returns a curried function.

filter.desc: Keeps elements of v for which function f returns a truthy value. Supports currying.

reduce.desc: Reduces v to a single value using a left fold with function f. Supports currying.

sort.desc: Stably sorts a list or array using natural ordering. Optionally accepts a custom comparator function. Supports currying.

keys.desc: Returns a List of all keys in a Dictionary.

values.desc: Returns a List of all values in a Dictionary.

hasKey.desc: Returns true if the Dictionary contains the specified key, false otherwise.

setUnion.desc: Returns a new Set containing all elements from both sets.

setIntersect.desc: Returns a new Set containing elements present in both sets.

print.desc: Prints arguments to the console, separated by spaces, without a trailing newline.

println.desc: Prints arguments to the console, separated by spaces, with a trailing newline.

readFile.desc: Reads the entire contents of a file into a string.

writeFile.desc: Writes a string to a file, overwriting existing content.

readCSV.desc: Reads a CSV file into a List of Lists.

pcall.desc: Executes a zero-argument function safely. Returns @[1, result] on success, @[0, errorMsg] on failure.

assert.desc: Throws an error if the condition is falsy.

gc.desc: Forces a Garbage Collection cycle. Returns the number of freed objects.

help.desc: Prints the main help overview or details for a specific topic.

run.desc: Executes a .jc2 script file in the current environment.

compileFile.desc: Compiles a .jc2 script file into bytecode and returns it as a callable function. Preserves relative path context.

compileCode.desc: Compiles a string of JC2 code into bytecode and returns it as a callable function.

sym.desc: Creates a symbolic variable for CAS operations.

diff.desc: Computes the symbolic or numerical derivative of an expression or function.

integ.desc: Computes the symbolic indefinite/definite integral, or numerical definite integral.

limit.desc: Computes the symbolic or numerical limit of an expression as var approaches val. Default is two-sided. dir can be "+" or "-". val can be "inf".

solveEq.desc: Symbolically solves an equation expr = 0 for the given variable.

subs.desc: Substitutes a variable with a value in a symbolic expression.

evalf.desc: Forces numerical floating-point evaluation of a symbolic expression.

json.encode.desc: Serializes a JC2 value into a JSON string.

json.decode.desc: Parses a JSON string into a JC2 value.

latex.to_latex.desc: Serializes a JC2 value (matrix, fraction, complex) into LaTeX code.

latex.eval.desc: Parses and evaluates a LaTeX math string directly.

image.img.desc: Allocates a new Image surface in RAM. Colors can be hex strings (e.g., "#FF0000") or names (e.g., "red").

width.desc: Returns the width of the image in pixels.

height.desc: Returns the height of the image in pixels.

setPixel.desc: Sets the color of a single pixel at (x, y).

getPixel.desc: Returns the color of the pixel at (x, y) as a hex string.

clear.desc: Fills the entire image with the specified color, or removes all elements from a Set, List, or Dict.

line.desc: Draws an anti-aliased line between two points.

rect.desc: Draws the outline of a rectangle.

text.desc: Renders text using a built-in 8x8 hardware font.

axes.desc: Draws Cartesian coordinate axes mapped to the specified range.

save.desc: Encodes and saves the image to a BMP file.

window.Window.desc: Creates a new hardware-accelerated OS window.

isOpen.desc: Returns true if the window is still open, false if closed.

pollEvent.desc: Pops the next input event from the window's queue. Returns a Dict or none.

isKeyDown.desc: Returns true if the specified physical key is currently pressed.

show.desc: Blits an Image object's buffer directly to the window.

setImeEnabled.desc: Enables or disables the OS Input Method Editor (IME) for the window.

showCursor.desc: Hides or shows the OS mouse cursor over the window.

setCursorPos.desc: Teleports the OS mouse cursor to the specified window coordinates.

pdf.desc: Returns the Probability Density Function (or PMF) evaluated at x.

cdf.desc: Returns the Cumulative Distribution Function evaluated at x.

quantile.desc: Returns the inverse CDF (quantile) for probability p (0 < p < 1).

sample.desc: Draws n random samples from the distribution and returns them as a row vector.

add.desc: Adds an element to a Set or List, or a key-value pair to a Dict.

remove.desc: Removes an element from a Set, an index from a List, or a key from a Dict. Throws an error if not found.

discard.desc: Removes an element from a Set or a key from a Dict silently (no error if not found).

eval.desc: Parses and evaluates a string as JC2 code.

charAt.desc: Returns the character at index i.

trim.desc: Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string.

find.desc: Returns the index of the first match of sub in s, or -1 if absent.

contains.desc: Returns true if sub is found in s, false otherwise.

concat.desc: Concatenates arbitrary types into a single string.

startsWith.desc: Returns true if string s starts with prefix.

endsWith.desc: Returns true if string s ends with suffix.

ord.desc: Returns the ASCII code of the first character of s.

chr.desc: Converts an ASCII code to a string.

parseNum.desc: Parses a string into a number (double or int).

first.desc: Returns the first element of a list or array.

last.desc: Returns the last element of a list or array.

shift.desc: Removes and returns the first element of a list (mutates) or array (returns first).

prepend.desc: Inserts a value at the beginning of a list or array.

insert.desc: Inserts a value at the specified index.

removeAt.desc: Removes the element at the specified index.

slice.desc: Extracts a slice of the container from start to end.

reverse.desc: Returns a reversed copy of the container or string.

flatten.desc: Recursively flattens nested containers into a 1D array or list.

unique.desc: Removes duplicate elements from a list or array.

indexOf.desc: Returns the first index of val in v, or -1 if absent.

count.desc: Counts the occurrences of val in v.

cumsum.desc: Returns the cumulative sum of the elements.

cumprod.desc: Returns the cumulative product of the elements.

diffs.desc: Returns the adjacent differences of the elements.

fill.desc: Creates an array with n copies of val.

linspace.desc: Generates n evenly-spaced points from a to b.

strmat.desc: Constructs a StringMatrix with r rows and c columns.

strfill.desc: Creates a 1xN StringMatrix filled with str.

strfind.desc: Finds a string in a StringMatrix, returning its [row, col] or -1.

strjoin.desc: Joins all elements of a StringMatrix with a delimiter.

strsort.desc: Sorts the elements of a StringMatrix lexicographically.

toStrMat.desc: Converts any matrix to a StringMatrix.

dictSize.desc: Returns the number of key-value entries in a Dict.

dictMerge.desc: Merges d2 into d1, overwriting existing keys.

dictPairs.desc: Returns a List of @[key, value] pairs from a Dict.

toList.desc: Converts an array, matrix, string, or set to a List.

toStrVec.desc: Converts a List or StringMatrix to a column StringMatrix.

toArray.desc: Converts a flat List to a numeric row vector.

toMatrix.desc: Converts a nested List to a Matrix.

zip.desc: Pair-wise merges two arrays or lists.

cat.desc: Concatenates multiple arrays or lists into one.

isinstance.desc: Checks if obj is an instance of cls (or any class if cls is omitted).

getClass.desc: Returns the class definition of an instance.

getParent.desc: Returns the parent class of a class definition.

setDiff.desc: Returns a Set of elements in a but not in b.

setSymDiff.desc: Returns a Set of elements in exactly one of the sets. Equivalent to the ^^ operator.

isSubset.desc: Returns true if a is a subset of b.

isSuperset.desc: Returns true if a is a superset of b.

isDisjoint.desc: Returns true if a and b share no elements.

setProduct.desc: Returns the Cartesian product of two sets.

setPow.desc: Returns the powerset of s (Set of all subsets).

appendFile.desc: Appends a string to the end of a file.

readLines.desc: Reads a file line-by-line into a List of strings.

writeLines.desc: Writes a List of elements as separate lines to a file.

fileExists.desc: Returns true if the file or directory exists, false otherwise.

fileSize.desc: Returns the physical file size in bytes.

listDir.desc: Returns a List of filenames in the specified directory.

readCSVMat.desc: Reads a CSV file directly into a StringMatrix.

parseCSVNum.desc: Reads a CSV file into a mathematical RealMatrix.

writeCSV.desc: Writes a Matrix or List out to a CSV file.

RootOf.desc: Represents the k-th exact root of the polynomial.

RootSum.desc: Represents the sum of expr evaluated over all roots of poly.

toFunc.desc: Compiles a symbolic AST to a blazing-fast VM closure.

evalv.desc: Evaluates a symbolic expression preserving exact types (Fraction/Complex).

replaceRule.desc: Pattern matching replacement in a symbolic expression.

factor.desc: Factors a polynomial, or returns a Dict of {Prime: Exponent} for an integer.

factorReal.desc: Factors a polynomial over the real numbers.

taylor.desc: Computes the Taylor series expansion of expr around a.

verifyInteg.desc: Verifies if the derivative of the integral matches the original expression.

isError.desc: Returns true if the pcall status array indicates an error.

resetConst.desc: Restores system constants PI, E, i, I.

pwd.desc: Prints the script directory and workspace directory.

imgPlot.signature: imgPlot(im, f, xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax, color, [thick])
imgPlot.desc: Plots a function f(x) onto an image canvas.

breakpoint.desc: Suspends VM execution and opens the interactive step-debugger.

disassemble.desc: Prints the bytecode disassembly of a function closure.

buildIndex.desc: Builds an O(1) anchor tree in RAM for the prime database.

mountPrimes.desc: Redirects the prime engine to a custom Prime.txt file.

sysinfo.desc: Prints current system and prime database status.

freeze.desc: Locks a container permanently, preventing modification.

isFrozen.desc: Returns true if the container is locked, false otherwise.

hash.desc: Returns the native hash value of x as an int.

clone.desc: Returns a deep-copied, fully unfrozen clone of the object.

copy.desc: Returns a deep-copied clone of the object, preserving its exact frozen/unfrozen state.

val.desc: Returns a deep-copied, fully frozen snapshot of the object.

symconfig.desc: Gets or sets CAS limits. Pass "default" to reset.

isbool.desc: Returns true if x is a boolean (true or false).

isint.desc: Returns true if x is an exact integer type (int, or Fraction with den=1).

iswhole.desc: Returns true if x is a whole number (int, integer-valued double, Fraction with den=1, or Complex with imag=0).

isfloat.desc: Returns true if x is a double.

isnumeric.desc: Returns true if x is any numeric type (including instances with math dunders).

iscomplex.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a Complex type.

isreal.desc: Returns true if x is a real number (imaginary part is 0).

isfrac.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a Fraction type.

isbase.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a BaseNum type.

isexact.desc: Returns true if x is an exact numeric type (int, Fraction, BaseNum, SymExpr).

isbinary.desc: Returns true if x is a boolean or 0.0/1.0.

ismatrix.desc: Returns true if x is any matrix type.

isrealmat.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a RealMatrix.

iscomplexmat.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a ComplexMatrix.

isstringmat.desc: Returns true if x is specifically a StringMatrix.

isvector.desc: Returns true if x is a 1D row or column vector.

issquare.desc: Returns true if x is a square matrix.

islist.desc: Returns true if x is a List.

isdict.desc: Returns true if x is a Dict.

isiterable.desc: Returns true if x supports for-in loops (has __iter__ or __next__).

iscallable.desc: Returns true if x can be called like a function (has __call__).

isindexable.desc: Returns true if x supports bracket indexing (has __getitem__).

ishashable.desc: Returns true if x can be used as a Dict key or Set element.

isstring.desc: Returns true if x is a String.

isalpha.desc: Returns true if all characters in s are alphabetic.

isdigit.desc: Returns true if all characters in s are digits.

isalnum.desc: Returns true if all characters in s are alphanumeric.

isspace.desc: Returns true if all characters in s are whitespace.

isupper.desc: Returns true if all alphabetic characters in s are uppercase.

islower.desc: Returns true if all alphabetic characters in s are lowercase.

isempty.desc: Returns true if the string, list, dict, or matrix is empty.

isnone.desc: Returns true if x is the none value.

isfunction.desc: Returns true if x is a function or closure.

isclass.desc: Returns true if x is a class definition.

isnamespace.desc: Returns true if x is a namespace.

issym.desc: Returns true if x is a Symbolic Expression.

isnan.desc: Returns true if x is NaN (Not a Number).

isinf.desc: Returns true if x is +/- Infinity.

isfinite.desc: Returns true if x is a finite number.

isprime.desc: Returns true if x is a prime number.

iseven.desc: Returns true if x is an even integer.

isodd.desc: Returns true if x is an odd integer.

isapprox.desc: Returns true if a and b are approximately equal within relative tolerance rtol (default 1e-9) and absolute tolerance atol (default 0.0).

iszero.desc: Returns true if x is equal to zero.

isset.desc: Returns true if x is a Set.

prob.Normal.desc: Constructs a Normal distribution N(mu, sigma^2).

prob.Uniform.desc: Constructs a Continuous Uniform distribution on [a, b).

prob.gamma.desc: Returns the Gamma function evaluated at x.

prob.lgamma.desc: Returns the natural logarithm of the absolute value of the Gamma function.

prob.betaFn.desc: Returns the Beta function evaluated at a and b.

prob.erfc.desc: Returns the complementary error function of x.

bytes.alloc.desc: Allocates a zeroed byte buffer of the specified size.

bytes.pack.desc: Creates a byte buffer from an array of 8-bit integers.

bytes.readFile.desc: Reads an entire file into a byte buffer.

bytes.writeFile.desc: Writes a byte buffer to a file.

bytes.set.desc: Writes a value into the buffer at the specified offset.

bytes.write_arr.desc: Directly copies an array into the buffer at C++ speeds.

bytes.get.desc: Reads a value from the buffer at the specified offset.

bytes.len.desc: Returns the total size of the buffer in bytes.

socket.connect.desc: Dials a TCP stream to the remote peer.

socket.send.desc: Sends a string over the TCP socket.

socket.recv.desc: Blocks and reads incoming packets from the socket.

socket.server.desc: Binds to a local interface and listens for incoming TCP connections.

socket.accept.desc: Blocks and accepts an incoming connection, returning a client socket.

subE.desc: Element-wise subtraction. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix.

mulE.desc: Element-wise multiplication. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix.

divE.desc: Element-wise division. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix.

idivE.desc: Element-wise integer division (truncating towards zero). Supports broadcasting.

powE.desc: Element-wise power. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix.

modE.desc: Element-wise modulo. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix.

eqE.desc: Element-wise equality comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

neqE.desc: Element-wise inequality comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

ltE.desc: Element-wise less-than comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

leE.desc: Element-wise less-than-or-equal comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

gtE.desc: Element-wise greater-than comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

geE.desc: Element-wise greater-than-or-equal comparison. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

maxE.desc: Element-wise maximum. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

minE.desc: Element-wise minimum. Supports scalar-scalar, scalar-matrix broadcasting, and matrix-matrix. Also supports strings.

orE.desc: Element-wise logical OR. Returns 1.0 if either is truthy, else 0.0.

xorE.desc: Element-wise logical XOR. Returns 1.0 if truthiness differs, else 0.0.

perm.desc: Returns the permanent of a square matrix.

setElement.desc: Returns a new matrix with the element at row r and column c set to val.

getR.desc: Extracts row r from a matrix.

getC.desc: Extracts column c from a matrix.

delR.desc: Deletes row r from a matrix.

delC.desc: Deletes column c from a matrix.

swapR.desc: Swaps row r1 and row r2 in a matrix.

swapC.desc: Swaps column c1 and column c2 in a matrix.

multiR.desc: Multiplies row r by a scalar.

multiC.desc: Multiplies column c by a scalar.

addC.desc: Adds scalar * column c2 to column c1.

cof.desc: Returns the cofactor of the element at row r and column c.

Acof.desc: Returns the algebraic cofactor of the element at row r and column c.

integD.desc: Returns the block diagonal concatenation of matrices A and B.

qr.desc: Returns a List @[Q, R] containing the orthogonal matrix Q and upper triangular matrix R from the QR decomposition of A.

lu.desc: Returns a List @[L, U, P] containing the lower triangular matrix L, upper triangular matrix U, and permutation matrix P from the LU decomposition of A.

residual.desc: Returns the residual vector r = b - A*x.

gcinfo.desc: Prints the current status of the Garbage Collector.

bool.desc: Converts a value to its boolean equivalent (true or false).

seq.desc: Generates a column vector sequence from start to end.

error.desc: Throws a runtime error with the specified message.

input.desc: Reads a line of text from standard input.

clock.desc: Returns the high-resolution time in seconds since the epoch.

sleep.desc: Pauses execution for the specified number of seconds.

highlight.desc: Returns a syntax-highlighted version of the JC2 code string.

color.desc: Enables ("on") or disables ("off") REPL syntax highlighting.

debugInteg.desc: Enables ("on") or disables ("off") verbose integration debug output.

removeKey.desc: Removes a key from a Dictionary. Throws an error if absent.

apply.desc: Calls function f with arguments unpacked from a list or array. Supports currying.

any.desc: Returns true if any element in v satisfies function f. Supports currying.

all.desc: Returns true if all elements in v satisfy function f. Supports currying.

countIf.desc: Counts the number of elements in v that satisfy function f. Supports currying.

solveE.desc: Numerically finds a root of f(x) = 0 near x0 using Newton-Raphson.

table.desc: Evaluates function f over a sequence or matrix of inputs.

setAdd.desc: Adds an element to a Set (legacy alias for add).

setRemove.desc: Removes an element from a Set (legacy alias for remove).

setDiscard.desc: Silently removes an element from a Set (legacy alias for discard).

setClear.desc: Clears all elements from a Set (legacy alias for clear).

setPop.desc: Removes and returns an arbitrary element from a Set.

matpow.desc: Computes the general matrix-to-matrix power: exp(B * ln(A)).

toSet.desc: Converts a list, array, or string into a Set, removing duplicates.

prob.dmean.desc: Returns the theoretical mean of a Distribution (global function variant).

prob.dvar.desc: Returns the theoretical variance of a Distribution (global function variant).

prob.dstd.desc: Returns the theoretical standard deviation of a Distribution (global function variant).

init.desc: Constructor method. Called automatically when a new class instance is created.
examples: init(x, y) = { self.x = x; self.y = y }

__add__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the addition operator (+).

__sub__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the subtraction operator (-).

__mul__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the multiplication operator (*).

__div__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the division operator (/).

__mod__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the modulo operator (%).

__pow__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the power operator (^).

__radd__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads reverse addition (other + self) when 'other' is not an instance.

__rmul__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads reverse multiplication (other * self) when 'other' is not an instance.

__neg__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the unary minus operator (-self).

__eq__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the equality operator (==).

__lt__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the less-than operator (<).

__contains__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the 'in' operator (val in self).

__setitem__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads index/key assignment (self[key] = val).

__str__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads string conversion (str(self), print, f-strings).

__len__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the len() function.

__abs__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads the abs() function.

__bool__.desc: Dunder method: Overloads truthiness evaluation (if, while, bool()).

__hash__.desc: Dunder method: Provides a hash value for Dict keys and Set elements. Must return a hashable type.

__iter__.desc: Dunder method: Returns an iterator object for for-in loops. Usually returns self.

__next__.desc: Dunder method: Returns the next value in an iteration, or none to stop.
examples: __next__() = { if (self.idx >= len(self.data)) return none; return self.data[self.idx++] }

__getattr__.desc: Dunder method: Intercepts access to non-existent properties (obj.key).

__setattr__.desc: Dunder method: Intercepts all property assignments (obj.key = val).

__call__.desc: Dunder method: Allows an instance to be called like a function.

for.signature: for (init; cond; update) { body }  |  for (var in iterable) { body }
desc: C-style for loop or for-in iteration loop.
C-style: for (init; condition; update) { body }
Executes init once, then repeats body while condition is truthy,
running update after each iteration.
For-in: for (var in iterable) { body }
Iterates over arrays, vectors, strings, lists, dicts, sets.
Supports destructuring: for ([k, v] in dict) { ... }
Supports local scope: for (local x in arr) { ... }
Braces {} are optional for single-statement bodies.
Note: The `(` MUST be on the same line as `for`.
See also: /help control
examples: for ([k, v] in {a: 1, b: 2}) print(k, v)

in.signature: for (var in iterable)  |  value in container
desc: Used in two contexts:
1. For-in loops: Iterates var over each element of an iterable.
Supported: arrays, vectors, strings, lists, dicts, sets.
2. Membership test (operator): Returns true if the value exists
in the container, false otherwise.
Supported: arrays, lists, strings, dicts (checks keys), sets,
and instances (checks __contains__, then fields, methods, and __getattr__).
See also: /help for, /help control
Immediately exits the innermost enclosing loop (for or while).
Cannot be used outside of a loop body.
See also: /help control
Skips the remainder of the current loop iteration and jumps
to the next iteration (or the condition check for while loops).
See also: /help control
examples: for (i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) { if (i % 2 == 0) continue; print(i) }

desc: Exits the current function and optionally returns a value.
If no expression is provided, returns `none`.
Note: `return` does NOT consume newlines. If you press Enter immediately
after `return`, it is treated as `return none`.
Can be used anywhere inside a function body, including nested blocks.
See also: /help control, /help scope
Pattern matching expression.
Evaluates the subject expression and matches it against a series of patterns.
Supports literal matching, variable binding, guard clauses, and deep destructuring
of lists, matrices, and dictionaries.
Use `,` to separate multiple patterns for a single branch.
Use `if (cond)` for guard clauses.
Use `_` as a wildcard or fallback pattern.
Returns the value of the executed branch, or `none` if no pattern matches.
See also: /help match (topic)
Pattern matching statement. Evaluates expr and compares against
each case value. Executes the first matching branch.
The switch body MUST be wrapped in {}.
Case branches do NOT require {} and absorb all statements until the next case.
Multiple values per case: `case val1, val2:`
No fall-through — only the matched branch executes.
Returns the value of the matched branch expression.
See also: /help control
A branch inside a `switch` statement.
Matches when the switch expression equals any of the listed values.
Multiple values can be comma-separated for a single branch.
Does NOT require {} and greedily absorbs statements until the next case/default/}.
See also: /help switch, /help control
The fallback branch inside a `switch` statement.
Executes when no `case` value matches the switch expression.
Does NOT require {} and greedily absorbs statements until the end of the switch.
See also: /help switch, /help control
Creates a namespace to group related functions and variables.
You can access its members using the dot operator (e.g., Name.member)
or bracket indexing (e.g., Name["member"]).
Variables declared with `local` are private and will not be exported.
★ Dynamic & Dict-Like:
Namespaces are fully dynamic. You can add, modify, or delete members
at runtime. They support all Dict operations (keys, values, for-in).
★ True Singleton & Freezing:
Namespaces share state perfectly. Exported `const` variables remain
strictly immutable. You can lock the entire namespace with `freeze()`
to make it hashable.
examples: namespace Math { local seed = 1; const PI = 3.14; add(a, b) = a + b }
for ([k, v] in Math) print(k, v)

desc: Defines a new class with methods and an optional constructor.
• `init(...)` is the constructor, called on instantiation.
• `self` refers to the current instance inside methods.
• Supports single inheritance via `extends`.
• Operator overloading via dunder methods (__add__, __str__, etc.).
Note: The class name MUST be on the same line as `class`.
See also: /help class (topic) for full details
examples: init(x, y) = { self.x = x; self.y = y }

desc: Declares that a class inherits from a parent class.
The child class inherits all methods from the parent.
Use `super.method()` to call the parent's implementation.
See also: /help class (topic)
Refers to the parent class's method implementation.
Typically used in constructors: `super.init(...)` to initialize
inherited fields, and in overridden methods to extend behavior.
See also: /help class (topic)
Refers to the current class instance inside a method body.
Used to read/write instance fields and call other methods.
Automatically available in all class methods — no declaration needed.
See also: /help class (topic)
Scope modifier: restricts a variable strictly to the current block.
Without `local`, variables automatically overflow to the function scope.
With `local`, the variable is forgotten when the enclosing `{}`, `if`,
or `for` block ends.
Usage forms:
local x = expr     Initialize block-scoped variable
local x += expr    Compound assignment to block-scoped variable
local x            Standalone declaration (defaults to none)
Works in destructuring (per-variable):
[local a, b] = [1, 2]       a is block-scoped, b is function-scoped
Works in loops:
for (local x in arr) { ... }
★ Closure Safety: If a lambda captures a local variable, its block
environment is safely preserved in memory.
See also: /help scope
Scope modifier: binds a variable to an OUTER scope variable.
Without `ref`, assignments inside functions create new auto-locals.
With `ref`, the assignment reads/writes the enclosing scope directly.
Usage forms:
ref x = expr       Assign to outer variable x (throws error on execution if x is absent)
ref x += expr      Compound assignment to outer variable (throws error on execution if x is absent)
ref x              Standalone declaration (silent on execution, throws error on subsequent use)
Works in destructuring (per-variable):
[ref a, b] = [1, 2]         a writes to outer, b is auto-local
{x: ref a, y: b} = obj      Same for dict destructuring
Also used for pass-by-reference parameters:
addOne(ref x) = { x = x + 1 }   Mutates the caller's variable
See also: /help scope, /help state
Scope modifier: gives a closure variable PRIVATE PERSISTENT memory.
Each call remembers the previous value of `state` variables,
but the outer scope variable (if any) remains completely untouched.
The initialization expression (e.g., state x = expr) is guaranteed
to evaluate and assign EXACTLY ONCE during the first execution.
Usage forms:
state x = expr     Evaluates expr EXACTLY ONCE. (e.g., state x = x captures outer x)
state x += expr    Captures outer x as initial state, then adds expr ON EVERY CALL
state x            Standalone declaration (captures outer 'x' at definition time).
If 'x' is undefined when the function is created, it will
throw an error IMMEDIATELY at definition time.
Works in destructuring (per-variable):
[state a, b] = [1, 2]    a has memory across calls, b resets each time
See also: /help scope, /help ref
examples: counter() = { state n = 0; n += 1; return n }

desc: Declares an immutable constant. Any attempt to reassign the variable
will throw a runtime error. Can still be removed with `delete`.
Constants declared inside functions or namespaces are locally scoped.
See also: /help scope
Removes a variable from the global scope entirely.
Works on any variable, including `const` and system constants.
For user function overloads, removes only the user-defined overload.
See also: /help scope
examples: delete PI         // use resetConst() to restore

desc: Error handling construct. Executes the body; if any error occurs,
execution jumps to the catch block with the error message in `var`.
try/catch is an expression — returns the value of whichever branch runs.
Control flow signals (break, continue, return) pass through unaffected.
See also: /help error
The error handler block of a `try` statement.
The variable receives the error message as a string.
You can re-throw the error with `throw e` to propagate it upward.
Note: The `(` MUST be on the same line as `catch`.
See also: /help try, /help error
Throws a runtime error with the given value (usually a string).
Unwinds the call stack until a `try/catch` block catches it.
If uncaught, prints a full stack trace and terminates execution.
See also: /help error
Loads and executes a .jc2 script or native C++ module.
Using `import module` automatically binds the loaded namespace to a variable.
Native modules (image, prob, json, bytes, socket, window, latex)
take priority over .jc2 files with the same name.
Importing the same module/file twice is a safe no-op (deduplicated).
See also: /help import (topic) for full details
Native boolean constant, acts as 1.0 in math.
It is a language keyword and cannot be overwritten or deleted.
See also: /help scope, /help control
Native boolean constant, acts as 0.0 in math.
It is a language keyword and cannot be overwritten or deleted.
See also: /help scope, /help control
Represents the absence of a value. Evaluates as falsy.
Functions without an explicit `return` return `none`.
It is a language keyword and cannot be overwritten or deleted.
See also: /help basic
